title.value: In-Processing fairness improvement methods for regression Data-Driven building Models: Achieving uniform energy prediction
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: In-Processing fairness improvement methods for regression Data-Driven building Models: Achieving uniform energy prediction

extractions.description: The paper proposes four in-processing methods—mean residual difference penalized (MRDP) regression, mean square error penalized (MSEP) regression, mean residual difference constrained (MRDC) regression, and mean square error constrained (MSEC) regression—to improve the predictive fairness of regression models for energy prediction in buildings, ensuring similar predictive performance across different conditions.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving energy prediction in buildings, which directly relates to sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Accurate energy prediction could also benefit suppliers in energy generation and distribution planning [9].

primary_category.justification: The primary focus is on energy prediction in buildings to achieve energy saving and cost saving.
primary_category.quote: Among these models, energy prediction models could be integrated into model predictive controller to provide optimal control signals for building energy management systems to achieve energy saving, cost saving, and/or peak shifting [8].

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper directly addresses improving energy efficiency in buildings through better prediction models.
primary_sub_category.quote: To improve the predictive fairness of regression models in terms of having similar predictive performance between different conditions, this study proposes four in-processing methods...
